newsitem.title: POLAND: Flood impact on Polish farms unknown until August.
newsitem.headline: Flood impact on Polish farms unknown until August.

text.p: The extent of damage to agriculture production caused by heavy rain and floods in southern Poland over the last week is still impossible to assess, the agriculture ministry said in a Friday statement.
"An assessment of the scope and size of production and infrastructure losses, as well as damage to housing, is currently impossible," the ministry statement said.
The ministry's view was supported by government spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowska, who told Reuters the damage would be known four weeks after the water subsides.
"The situation can be reviewed, according to experts, four weeks after the water is gone, so if the flood ends in mid-July we should know the data by mid-August," Jakubowska said.
Torrential rain has caused floods which put more than 350,000 hectares or one percent of Poland under water killing at least 23 people and forcing thousands out of their homes.
Jakubowska also said that despite the damage to agriculture due to the floods Poland will not need to import any additional food, because it had large reserves.

An official from the Meteorology and Water Management Institute, who makes harvest estimates, said that so far there was no precise information on the size of the inundated growing areas for various crops.
